cards.back: Central Processing Unit — the hardware that executes program instructions.
RAM is volatile read-write working memory that loses content when power is off; ROM is non-volatile read-only memory holding permanent start-up instructions.
A finite, ordered set of unambiguous steps for solving a problem.

cards.front: What is system software? Give one example.
cards.back: Software that manages the computer itself, e.g. an operating system like Linux or Windows.
Software that performs a task for the user, e.g. a word processor or browser.

cards.front: One kilobyte equals how many bytes?
Name the two main parts of the CPU.
cards.back: The Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU) and the Control Unit (CU).

cards.front: What is a high-level programming language?
cards.back: A language close to human English (like Python or Java) that must be translated to machine code before a computer runs it.

cards.front: What does an operating system do?
cards.back: It manages hardware resources and provides services to application programs — memory, files, processes and input/output.
Hardware is the physical equipment you can touch; software is the set of instructions that runs on it.
